title: Telemetry — Activation/Retention Event Contract
description: The COMPLETE, EXHAUSTIVE field set any event telemetry.events.record_mission_completion() ever writes may contain. This is the technical enforcement of the privacy contract in docs/TELEMETRY.md, not just a documentation promise: additionalProperties:false means telemetry.store.append_event() raises telemetry.consent.TelemetryError (schema_check.SchemaValidationError, wrapped) rather than writing ANY record carrying an undocumented field -- spec text, plan content, entity/user names, file paths, or any other free-form or identifying string are not merely discouraged, they are IMPOSSIBLE to write through this contract without a code change to this file itself (which tests/telemetry/test_events_privacy.py would then have to be updated to match, in full view of review). See intent-router/schema/routing-decision.schema.json for this repo's own established precedent of the same additionalProperties:false discipline.

schema.description: Contract version tag, mirroring intent_router's own 'schema' field convention.

event_id.description: Opaque unique id for this event (uuid4 hex string) -- identifies the EVENT RECORD, never a person or a piece of content. The pattern is [Cyra LOW-1]'s enforced shape: exactly 32 lowercase hex characters (uuid.uuid4().hex's own format), rejecting anything else -- including a well-formed-looking-but-non-hex or non-32-length string -- regardless of what a future caller passes in, not merely the shape today's one caller (telemetry.events.record_mission_completion()) happens to produce.

event_type.description: 'activation' -- this install's FIRST completed governed mission (mission_ordinal == 1: a human approval -> a finalized spec -> a generated app, the full accountability chain, firing once). 'retention' -- every governed mission completed after the first (mission_ordinal >= 2).

timestamp.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp with millisecond precision and a 'Z' suffix, the exact shape telemetry.consent.utc_now_iso() produces (mirroring intent_router.types.utc_now_iso() / spec_engine.content.utc_now_iso()'s own convention). [Cyra LOW-1]: the pattern enforces this exact shape -- a bare-seconds, non-'Z', or non-'T'-separated timestamp is rejected here, not merely discouraged by convention.

install_id.description: A LOCALLY-GENERATED, RANDOM (uuid4) anonymous identifier for this opted-in install -- never derived from hostname, MAC address, OS username, IP address, or any other identifying machine/account property. Written once by telemetry.consent.enable() and re-used across a disable/re-enable cycle so retention counts stay attributable to one install; a fresh 'delete' (telemetry.store.delete_all()) followed by a fresh 'enable' generates a brand-new one. Same enforced 32-lowercase-hex pattern as `event_id` above.

mission_ordinal.description: A coarse count: this event is the Nth governed mission this install has completed (1 for the activation event, 2+ for every retention event). Never a spec_id, plan_id, or any other content-derived slug.

days_since_last_mission.description: Wall-clock days between THIS mission's completion and the immediately preceding one (round-tripped through datetime, not wall-clock-drift-sensitive beyond that) -- null for the activation event (mission_ordinal == 1, there is no prior mission to measure a gap from).

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by telemetry.schema_check: type, enum, properties, required, additionalProperties, pattern. ('minimum'/'minLength' above are documentation only, same as intent-router/schema/routing-decision.schema.json's own 'confidence' field -- the shared minimal-validator design does not enforce numeric/string-length bounds; additionalProperties:false and, as of [Cyra LOW-1], the 'pattern' on event_id/install_id/timestamp are the keywords here that are load-bearing for the privacy guarantee, and they ARE enforced -- see telemetry/schema_check.py's own module docstring for the re.search() semantics.)
